properties.accessible_reason: The ground state of Cr2 (X 1Sigma_g+) is a formal sextuple bond built from 12 electrons (sigma^2 pi^4 delta^4 plus 4s sigma^2), which requires a multi-reference treatment. Neither of the two levels of theory permitted for this task can describe it: PM7 converges to a restricted closed-shell singlet (the 12 unpaired electrons are not represented), is not size consistent along the dissociation coordinate and switches SCF solutions between neighbouring geometries; GFN2-xTB gives a WBO of only 4.28, a HOMO-LUMO gap of 0.02 eV and a dissociation energy 4.3x the experimental value. Both methods are 27-47% off in r_e and both get omega_e wrong. A bond dissociation energy from either method therefore cannot be stood behind.
properties.bond_dissociation_energy_kcal_mol: not declared (accessible=false) - no value at the two allowed levels of theory can be stood behind. Exploratory values, kept only to document how badly the methods fail: GFN2-xTB D_e = 141.8 kcal/mol (6.15 eV) = E(GFN2 10 A restricted-singlet point, xtb/sp/cr2_10.00/sp.log, -3.495514166 Ha) - E(GFN2 minimum r = 2.12867 A, xtb/ohess/ohess.log, -3.721548858 Ha); that asymptote is size consistent with 2xE(Cr, uhf 0) to 0.33 kcal/mol, but the value is 4.3x the experimental D_0. GFN2 atom-sum estimate (also exploratory): D_e' = 2xE(Cr, uhf 0) - E(min) = 142.2 kcal/mol. PM7 gives no self-consistent BDE at all: depending on which SCF solution / geometry is used it scatters from -312.8 kcal/mol (2xE(Cr, 7S) = 0.302784 Ha - E(min); PM7 orders the atoms correctly, so this is a legitimate PM7 atom-sum estimate and says PM7 even predicts Cr2 to be unbound) through -83.4 kcal/mol (against 2xE(Cr, closed-shell) = 0.668364 Ha) to +213.7 kcal/mol (against the literal 10 A point, which is a maximum with one imaginary mode of -17.13 cm^-1).

experimental_reference.note: Gas-phase Cr2 X 1Sigma_g+ reference values used only as an accuracy yardstick; not computed in this project.

potential_energy_curve.description: Ground-state (charge 0, multiplicity 1, gas phase) Cr2 potential energy curve computed with the two permitted levels of theory: rigid fixed-geometry single points on the z axis (no constraint, no relaxation), one unchanged native log per point (see each point's 'log'). These are raw single-point energies along the Cr-Cr coordinate, not stationary-point claims.
potential_energy_curve.units: r in Angstrom; energies in Hartree (absolute, as printed by the program)
potential_energy_curve.assessment: PM7: steep wall below 2.0 A, a local minimum at 2.4679 A (0.80129 Ha), a non-monotonic middle section with SCF-solution switches (2.80 A = 0.72452 and 2.90 A = 0.70511 lie 0.08-0.10 Ha BELOW the 3.00-4.00 A points), a flat tail around 0.844 Ha from 4 to 8 A and a jump of +0.298 Ha at 10 A with one imaginary mode (-17.13 cm^-1) - i.e. no consistent dissociation asymptote. GFN2-xTB: monotonic rise after the minimum at 2.15 A with a very soft long tail (plateau 2.5-2.7 A), no barrier, but the dissociation energy is 4.3x the experimental value. Neither curve reproduces the experimental r_e, omega_e or D_0.
potential_energy_curve.per_point_logs: every point carries its own unchanged native log in the 'log' field; absolute paths are relative to the sandbox root

properties.evidence_smiles_annotation: every input/log carries the line 'smiles: [Cr][Cr]' (dimer) or 'smiles: [Cr]' (atom)

properties.accessible_reason: The two-atom dissociation limit of the singlet curve is not a clean, consistent minimum at either allowed level of theory. Physical asymptote: the sum of two ground-state atoms, E(2xCr, 7S). The only genuine singlet-asymptote stationary point is the GFN2-xTB restricted-singlet r = 10 A flat point (2.12 cm^-1, 0 imaginary, size consistent with 2xE(Cr, uhf 0) to -0.33 kcal/mol), obtained with a frozen Cr-Cr coordinate. PM7 has no asymptote at all: its long-range stationary point at r = 6.9786 A is a plateau extremum that lies 0.5411 Ha above 2xE(Cr, 7S) and 0.1755 Ha above 2xE(Cr, closed-shell), and the literal r = 10 A point is a maximum (one imaginary mode, -17.13 cm^-1) reached by an SCF-solution switch.

pm7_long_range.note: PM7 long-range plateau extremum only. It is NOT the species asymptote energy: it lies 340 kcal/mol above 2xE(Cr, 7S) and 110 kcal/mol above 2xE(Cr, closed-shell), so no PM7 BDE may be quoted from it.

gfn2_xtb_10A.note: single point of the two Cr atoms 10 A apart (restricted closed-shell singlet, --uhf 0); the constrained optimization + Hessian at the same distance gives -3.495516248 Ha with a 2.12 cm^-1 real mode and zero imaginary modes (xtb/asym_ohess/ohess.log), i.e. the same asymptote 0.0013 kcal/mol away

atomic_limit.note: PM7 orders the Cr atoms correctly: mult 7 (7S, sp_cr_atom_mult7.log) = 0.151392137 Ha lies 114.70 kcal/mol BELOW mult 1 (sp_cr_atom_mult1.log) = 0.334182041 Ha. Only GFN2-xTB inverts the ordering: uhf 0 (-1.747497514 Ha) lies 54.66 kcal/mol below uhf 6 (-1.660416971 Ha).

properties.accessible_note: A single Cr atom is computable at both allowed methods. PM7 reproduces the 7S < closed-shell ordering correctly; only GFN2-xTB inverts it (see atomic_state_ordering_error).
properties.description: Atomic reference species for the dissociation limit of the singlet dimer: the product node Cr2_asymptote ([Cr].[Cr]) is the pair of these atoms. It is kept as its own node so that the atom-sum estimate D_e' = 2*E(Cr) - E(Cr2 minimum) is a first-class graph quantity rather than a number hidden in prose. It carries no elementary step of its own (the only transformation in this graph, the Cr-Cr cleavage, is already recorded as edge e1).

frequencies.pm7_mult7: three zero frequencies only (free translations), NImag = 0
frequencies.note: single-atom frequency jobs give no 3N-6 internal modes

properties.atomic_state_ordering_error: PM7 gets the Cr atomic spectrum right: the septet (7S, 3d5 4s1) lies 114.70 kcal/mol BELOW the closed-shell atom (0.151392137 vs 0.334182041 Ha). GFN2-xTB inverts it: uhf 0 (-1.747497514 Ha) lies 54.66 kcal/mol below uhf 6 (-1.660416971 Ha). The physical ground state is 7S, so any BDE built from GFN2 atoms inherits this error, while the PM7 atom-sum estimate (-312.8 kcal/mol, Cr2 unbound) is legitimate for the PM7 model.

edges.channel: homolytic Cr-Cr bond dissociation (ground-state singlet surface)

properties.barrier: none: the singlet Cr2 curve is purely dissociative - its only stationary points are the bound minimum and the separated-atom limit, so no first-order saddle of the elementary step exists on the Cr-Cr coordinate and no IRC can be defined. The shallow PM7 tail extrema (r = 5.736 A, 27.97 cm^-1; r = 6.9786 A, 13.86 cm^-1), the r = 4.013 A point with one imaginary mode (-58.05 cm^-1) and the r = 10 A maximum (-17.13 cm^-1) are numerical artefacts of a non-size-consistent curve, not transition states.
properties.note: Bond order of the Cr-Cr pair decreases from the formally sextuple bond of the singlet minimum to zero at the dissociation limit, hence the pair is recorded in 'break'.
properties.barrier_note_kcal_mol: not applicable (no barrier of the elementary step; see 'barrier')
